short: Four years of industrialised attrition that destroyed four empires.
full:
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914 triggered a chain of alliance obligations that converted a Balkan crisis into a continental war within five weeks. Both sides expected it to be over by Christmas.

Instead, machine guns, barbed wire and quick-firing artillery gave the defence an overwhelming advantage, and the Western Front froze into 700 kilometres of trenches for four years. Around 20 million people died. The war brought tanks, aircraft and chemical weapons into general use, and ended the Russian, German, Austro-Hungarian and Ottoman empires. The armistice took effect at 11am on 11 November 1918; the settlement at Versailles left grievances that helped produce the next war twenty years later.
